sector_model: regulated gas utility (fiscal year ends Sep 30); use earnings, rate base growth, allowed returns, regulatory lag, equity and debt funding, dividend; negative free cash flow is structural, not a defect by itself; FCF yield not used
thesis: Atmos Energy is a natural-gas-only distributor (about 3.4M customers, eight states, Texas concentrated) that earned 8.49 diluted EPS (about 1.4B net income) in fiscal 2026 and guides fiscal 2027 to 9.05-9.25 (+7% to +9% at the midpoint over 8.49) with 4.5B of capital spending and a dividend raised 9.0% to 4.36. At 173.22 (2026-11-06) it trades at 20.4x fiscal 2026 EPS and 18.9x the guidance midpoint, 1.9x June book value per share, with a 2.5% dividend yield. Fiscal 2026 capex was 4.2B, over 85% safety and reliability, largely under regulatory mechanisms with recovery lag of six months or less; 26B planned for fiscal 2026-2030. At 6/30/2026 equity capitalization was 59.8%, debt to capitalization 41% against a 70% covenant, and no commercial paper was outstanding.
counterthesis: Growth is funded by outside capital, not internal cash: 9M26 operating cash flow was 1.67B against 3.08B of capex (free cash flow about -1.40B) and 0.49B of dividends, so the company issued 1.30B of debt and 0.94B of equity in nine months; shares outstanding rose from 161.6M to 169.0M (+4.6%) in nine months, so EPS growth of about 8-9% is a per-share figure earned on a growing share count. Debt rose to 10.3B from 9.0B. Rate base growth only translates to earnings if Texas, Louisiana and other regulators keep approving recovery and allowed returns; political pressure on affordability, higher rates on refinancing and a full valuation (about 19-20x for a utility) leave little room. The stock is up from about 164 in mid-October. Year-end fiscal 2026 balance sheet, 10-K audit matters, regulatory asset detail, allowed ROE by jurisdiction and rating agency metrics were not read. Peer utility multiples not gathered.
invalidation: Rate case or infrastructure-mechanism outcomes that cut allowed returns or delay recovery beyond one year; funds from operations to debt falling toward rating-downgrade thresholds; debt to capitalization above 50%; fiscal 2027 EPS tracking below 9.05; equity issuance running above the 4-5% annual share growth seen in fiscal 2026; a pipeline-safety incident with unrecoverable costs.
